newsitem.title: UK: BT takes stake in France's Cegetel.
newsitem.headline: BT takes stake in France's Cegetel.

text.p: British Telecommunications (BT) said it had agreed with Compagnie Generale des Eaux to take a 25 percent stake in Cegetel, a new French telecoms group, for 1.1 billion stg in cash and the share capital of BT France.
BT said in a statement that other partners in Cegetel would include SBC, formerly South Western Bell, and Germany's Mannesmann.
BT said its participation in Cegetel was likely to be "marginally earnings dilutive in the short-term but is expected to have significant long-term benefits."

The new group will provide the full range of telecoms services in France, BT said, with mobile through SFR, in which Vodafone has a stake. Cegetel will apply for a licence for a full range of telephony services from January 1, 1998.
"The talks were short and mostly sweet -- underlining the compatibility of the two companies," BT chief executive Sir Peter Bonfield said in a statement.
The deal had been widely rumoured in the media after BT and CGE announced on Wednesday parallel press conferences for later on Thursday.
